subject: Nariway Daily Check-in - 2026-08-18
html:
Nariway Daily Check-in

18 August 2026

Needs your attention / action today

  • Post the first Substack Note. The queue is playbook-clean (CMO steward fixed all four closings this week), and it has sat ready and unposted for four straight days while Query A is live and drawing eyes to the publication. Both the CFO and CMO stewards name this as the single highest-leverage move outstanding.
  • Confirm whether nariway.com's interim art-collections copy is actually live. This week's first site-health run found Google's index still shows the old "Hidden History of Work" identity site-wide. If the swap never went live, that is the fix; if it did, this is a reindex-only request. Either way, a Qwoted respondent googling Nariway right now may land on the wrong site.
  • Log Query A responses as they land. The response window is open and the Intelligence Log is still empty.
  • One fact only you know: does your bio say "more than 100 museums" or "hundreds of museums"? website.md and positioning.md still disagree.
  • A QA finding not yet acted on: the live, published Substack About/Welcome copy runs several short parallel sentences and subject-less fragments in a row, against the house voice rules against staccato sequences. Worth a look next time either page is touched, since it is live public copy.

Today I learned

Sotheby's and Christie's are not just auction houses anymore, they are art lenders, and the same house can be both the lender and the eventual seller of the collateral. Sotheby's Financial Services' own loan book grew from $800M to $1.6B since 2021 (doubling in four years); Christie's Art Finance is estimated near $500M. Both advance against a work's low auction estimate, and if the collateral's value falls and breaches the agreed loan-to-value ratio, the borrower faces a margin call or a forced sale, typically at auction, through the same institution that made the loan. It is a live version of the "independence" problem the report already names for private banks. Source note: market-intelligence #7.

What changed, and what it means

  • Two report chapters got their first real sourcing. Art finance (loan terms, and the lender/seller conflict above) and institutional economics ("why museums say no": a 90-95% gift-rejection rate, a live Philadelphia Museum of Art deficit, AAM's 2025 sector survey). The report's ecosystem sections are filling in even while case-coding holds at 50 of 50.
  • QA caught its own headline statistic losing its caveat in transit. The 13-of-13-vs-10-of-13 governance-survival figure had lost its "hand-selected sample, not a population rate" caveat in HOME and the learnings log. Fixed in both today, source of truth unchanged.
  • Site-health's first-ever run confirmed a live CRITICAL, not just a suspected one: Google's index of nariway.com still surfaces the old identity, the exact scenario flagged as costing a Qwoted conversation.
  • Network research filed six new partner leads, two events, and two board candidates to the warm network and board-opportunities shortlist.
  • Signals filed a new prospect, Joop van Caldenborgh (Museum Voorlinden), a rare living founder on the record about a legacy he has already executed, not just discussed.
  • The recurring drift: the day the response window actually opened, founder time went back to research and writing rather than commercial validation, per the CFO steward.

Where we stand

Query A's response window has now been open for two full days with the Intelligence Log still empty, so there is still no real data point on whether anyone will pay (H7B), only the wait itself. The report's core statistic almost reached you and future readers without its caveat this week, worth remembering as the flagship report gets closer to outside eyes: precision on the way in has to survive the trip out. Still $0 earned; the moves above are how that starts to change.
